The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

The vectors $\mathbf e_\theta$ and $\mathbf e_\varphi$ are orthonormal, transverse to $\mathbf n$, and satisfy $\mathbf n\times\mathbf e_\theta=\mathbf e_\varphi$ and $\mathbf n\times\mathbf e_\varphi=-\mathbf e_\theta$. Thus $e_\sigma$ has unit norm and $h e_\sigma=\sigma e_\sigma$; multiplication by the phase $e^{i\sigma\varphi}$ preserves both properties. This identity fixes the phase contribution of the chosen gauge under the rotation convention in [F3].

derivations.claim: For any nonempty bounded open interval $(u,v)$, choose $c$ and $\varepsilon>0$ with $[c-\varepsilon,c+\varepsilon]\subset(u,v)$. Apply [F2] in $\mathbb R^3$ with radii $\varepsilon/2<\varepsilon$, obtaining a smooth $\rho$ equal to $1$ on the smaller ball and supported in the larger. The restriction $g(x)=\rho((x-c)e_1)$ is smooth, equals $1$ on a neighborhood of $c$, and is supported in $(u,v)$. Applying this construction to $(\kappa_-,\kappa_+)$ and $(\theta_1,\theta_2)$ gives the required nonzero functions $a$ and $b$.

The integrand $|a(r)|^2|b(\theta)|^2$ is bounded and supported in a finite radial annulus and a finite-measure spherical chart, so it is integrable. By [F1], [F3], and [F4],
$$\|f^0_{\sigma,\ell}\|_\nu^2=\frac12\left(\int_{\kappa_-}^{\kappa_+}r|a(r)|^2\,dr\right)\left(\int_{S^2}|b(\theta)|^2\,d\Omega\right)=\pi AB.$$
The first factor $A$ is finite and positive because $a$ is bounded, compactly supported, and equals $1$ on an interval. The spherical chart gives $\int_{S^2}|b(\theta)|^2d\Omega=2\pi B$, so $B$ is finite and positive for the same reason. Thus $0<\|f^0_{\sigma,\ell}\|_\nu^2=\pi AB<\infty$, and the stated normalization is valid.

The support lies in $\kappa_-<r<\kappa_+$ and $\theta_1<\theta<\theta_2$, a compact region away from $\mathbf k=0$ and the azimuthal axis after taking the compact supports of $a,b$. The frame $e_\sigma^N$ is smooth and transverse with $P_\sigma e_\sigma^N=e_\sigma^N$ by [F1]; because $\ell$ is integral, $e^{i\ell\varphi}$ is single-valued and smooth on this region. Extension by zero is smooth since $a,b$ have compact support in the open intervals. Hence $f^0_{\sigma,\ell}\in\mathcal D$, and dividing by its positive norm preserves membership and helicity while giving norm one.

Under $R_z(-t)$, $r$ and $n_z$ stay fixed and $\varphi$ becomes $\varphi-t$. Therefore [F1] gives $U(R_z(t))f_{\sigma,\ell}=e^{-i\ell t}e^{-i\sigma t}f_{\sigma,\ell}=e^{-i(\ell+\sigma)t}f_{\sigma,\ell}$. Since $f_{\sigma,\ell}\in\mathcal D\subseteq D(J_z)$ by [F5], differentiating at $t=0$ in the Stone convention of [F5] yields $J_zf_{\sigma,\ell}=(\ell+\sigma)\hbar f_{\sigma,\ell}$.
